summary: The note argues that urban green spaces are social hubs as well as environmental assets, fostering community cohesion. It covers inclusive park design, community gardens, playgrounds, health benefits, economic effects, festivals and co-creation, with quotes and dates from experts and residents between September 2023 and May 2024.
one_line: Urban green spaces such as parks, community gardens and playgrounds act as social, health and economic hubs that strengthen community cohesion.
key_facts: Professor Emily Grant, an environmental psychologist at Metro University, said on October 5 that urban green spaces are 'shared living rooms for the community'.
A municipal initiative announced on September 15, 2023 encourages cities to use innovative designs to make green spaces more inclusive.

On November 12, landscape architect Josephine Mendoza unveiled a new park in the city's East End with an amphitheater, community gardens, and intertwining paths meant to encourage incidental meetings among neighbors.
The community garden on West Maple Avenue, established in late September 2023, has seen a noticeable uplift in neighborhood interaction.
Local resident David Kim called the West Maple Avenue garden 'a meeting place' where people can slow down, talk and reconnect.
A December 2023 survey by the City Parks Association found that 87% of parents and guardians felt playgrounds were essential for fostering social connections among families.
Survey participant Jenny Patel said she met most of her local friends at the playground.
The Green Ribbon campaign was initiated on January 18, 2024 to spotlight the role of parks in encouraging healthier lifestyles.
Dr. Sara Johannson's review, published February 10, 2024, outlines how regular interaction with green spaces can reduce stress, improve concentration and encourage physical activity.
A March 3, 2024 joint study by the Commerce Chamber and the Environmental Coalition found proximity to green spaces can increase property values, attract tourism and bolster local economies.
The annual Spring Flora Festival, launched April 25, 2024 in Oak Park, lets locals showcase cultural heritage through food, music and dance.
Urban community organizer Lucas Chang said at a May 15, 2024 stakeholder meeting, 'People take care of what they help to create,' supporting co-creation of parks.
